clue.text: House destruction averted, remember? Remember when!

definitions.text: House destruction averted, remember? Remember when!

parts.words: House destruction averted, remember? Remember when!
parts.note: the date of the foiled Gunpowder Plot to blow up the Houses of Parliament, recalled in the rhyme beginning 'Remember, remember'

explanation.surface: A nostalgic prompt to recall a narrow escape for some building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot of 1605 aimed to blow up the Houses of Parliament; Britain marks its failure with bonfires and fireworks, and the rhyme starts 'Remember, remember'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes Night commemorates the day the plot against Parliament was foiled.

clue.text: The banks went bust — liquidity problem followed!

definitions.text: The banks went bust — liquidity problem followed!

parts.words: The banks went bust — liquidity problem followed!
parts.note: reads as a financial crash, but the banks are riverbanks giving way and the liquidity is water spilling over

explanation.surface: A banking collapse leads to a cash-flow crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial words mislead: 'banks' are the sides of a river and 'liquidity' is literal water.
explanation.definitionFit: When river banks burst, the surrounding land is under water, swamped by the overflow.

clue.text: Certainly not advised to do it on passing-out parade

definitions.text: Certainly not advised to do it on passing-out parade

parts.words: Certainly not advised to do it on passing-out parade
parts.note: a passing-out parade is a graduation ceremony for cadets, but passing out also means losing consciousness

explanation.surface: Advice to graduating cadets about what not to do at their ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: A passing-out parade is the British military graduation march; collapsing on it would be literal 'passing out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to lose consciousness briefly, which is what passing out means.

clue.text: Dropped round during a storm

parts.note: sounds like someone calling in on a visit in bad weather, but describes a round pellet of ice falling

explanation.surface: Someone paid a visit while the weather was wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped round' suggests a social call; here it is a round thing that drops from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail falls as small round balls of ice during storms.

clue.text: TV fee is upsetting, but makes us cheerful

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so these letters are tipped over into a new order

explanation.surface: Paying the television licence is annoying, yet it keeps us happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges TVFEEIS; 'is' belongs to the fodder, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive means jolly and celebratory, as in a holiday mood.

clue.text: Love cookers? But these aren't apples

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O
ranges are large kitchen stoves

explanation.surface: Someone fond of stoves notes these are not apples.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on comparing apples and oranges: a fruit that is not an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial contrast with apples is the citrus fruit in the saying about unlike things.

clue.text: We've done remarkably well to do this!

definitions.text: We've done remarkably well to do this!

parts.words: We've done remarkably well to do this!
parts.note: describes an act of outstanding performance from the point of view of the achiever

explanation.surface: A proud boast after a great achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine or outdo others is to perform exceptionally well.

clue.text: Were biers ordered from them? It sounds logical

definitions.text: Were biers ordered from them? It sounds logical

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged, so the letters are put in a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Were coffin stands bought from beer makers? The names make it seem sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges WEREBIERS; the joke is that biers (coffin stands) sound like beers, which come from these places.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is made in brewing plants, so beers would logically be ordered from them.

clue.text: It's your duty to be listed on them

definitions.text: It's your duty to be listed on them

parts.words: It's your duty to be listed on them
parts.note: a duty here is a shift of work assigned on a rota, and the lists show who does which shift

explanation.surface: A reminder that being on the list is an obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' means a scheduled shift, not a moral obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotas are schedules naming who is on duty at what time.

clue.text: The gold one drinks starts here

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral for one
gins are spirit drinks

explanation.surface: Here is where the golden drinker's habit began.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginnings or sources are the points from which things begin.

clue.text: Bowed to the might of Henry V's army

definitions.text: Bowed to the might of Henry V's army

parts.words: Bowed to the might of Henry V's army
parts.note: seems to describe enemies submitting, but means soldiers armed with bows, the strength of Henry V's force at Agincourt

explanation.surface: Enemies submitted to the power of an English king's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowed' looks like 'bent in submission' but means 'equipped with bows'; English longbowmen won Agincourt for Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen with longbows formed the decisive part of Henry V's army at Agincourt.

clue.text: Running checks on half the side, and hating it

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another means placed after it
half of the word side, the back half of its four letters

parts.note: running checks is testing

explanation.surface: Inspecting part of a team and loathing the task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like a team to be tested, but only its back half is used, with 'on' meaning placed after in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, so the present participle means loathing.

clue.text: Be prone, for example, to back a lord

parts.note: to be prone is to lie flat

indicators.note: to back means going backwards, so the abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: Lying down, say, in support of a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reads as supporting the lord, but it is the signal turning the abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal superior to whom vassals owed allegiance is their lord.

clue.text: Disapprove of feeling that you do so

definitions.text: Disapprove of feeling that you do so

parts.words: Disapprove of feeling that you do so
parts.note: describes strongly condemning something, the feeling of disapproval itself

explanation.surface: A remark about being uneasy with one's own disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn or regret strongly is to express disapproval of something.

clue.text: Carried no driver

parts.note: sounds like a vehicle with nobody at the wheel, but describes someone carried who is not doing the driving

explanation.surface: A vehicle travelled without anyone at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'carried' as a noun-like description: someone carried who is not the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in a vehicle who is not operating it is carried along as a rider.

clue.text: Liquor with no body!

definitions.meaning: strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin

explanation.surface: A drink so thin it lacks any substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no body' means bodiless, as ghosts are, not a weak wine lacking body.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled drinks are called this, and so are ghosts, beings without physical form.

clue.text: Trouble for the Chancellor caused by a blow?

definitions.meaning: rising prices are a worry for the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister
blowing air into a balloon or tyre expands it

explanation.surface: A financial headache for a minister arising from some setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK finance minister; 'blow' is a breath of air, not a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rising prices in an economy and filling something with air.

clue.text: Lay out money in America, then stop for the time being

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation sits inside the word for paying out

parts.note: to lay out money is to spend
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Spend cash in the States, then pause for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in America' looks like the setting for spending; it is a container signal putting the country's abbreviation within the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something temporarily, meaning to defer it, is to put it on hold.

clue.text: Makes oneself comfortable in furniture?

definitions.meaning: to get cosy and relaxed in a place
a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

explanation.surface: Getting cosy among the chairs and sofas.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is an old wooden bench with arms and a high back.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means getting comfortable, and the noun names wooden benches.

clue.text: Medic points to bandages

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medic
compass points E, S, S, E and S

explanation.surface: The doctor indicates the dressings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' supplies a string of compass points E, S, S, E, S.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind a wound with a covering is to treat it with a protective wrap.

clue.text: Got out trigger happy member of the Bomb Squad then

definitions.text: Got out trigger happy member of the Bomb Squad then

parts.words: Got out trigger happy member of the Bomb Squad then
parts.note: suggests a reckless soldier dismissed, but describes the trigger of a bomb being taken out so the device is made safe

explanation.surface: A gun-crazy bomb disposal officer was thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trigger happy' misleads: the trigger is removed, making the bomb safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a bomb harmless by removing its fuse or trigger is the bomb squad's job.

clue.text: Rob lopsided absurdity-get away with 500

indicators.note: absurdity means nonsense, so these letters are jumbled into another order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A ridiculous lopsided robbery that got away with five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LOPSIDED, less a D (500) taken out by 'get away with', are rearranged by 'absurdity'.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder or strip of valuables means to steal from someone.

clue.text: See what it means

parts.note: to perceive the meaning of something, to make it out

explanation.surface: An invitation to look up a meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive or make out the sense of something is to see it clearly.

clue.text: In Notts, runs the council. That's all over now

definitions.meaning: a river that flows through Nottinghamshire, an English county

definitions.text: the council. That's all over now
definitions.meaning: the sixteenth-century Church council held in the Italian city of that name, long since concluded

explanation.surface: Notes on who controls the local authority before it is abolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' is a river flowing, not running the council; Notts is Nottinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Midlands river and to the Counter-Reformation council of 1545 to 1563.

clue.text: One digging in the rose garden?

definitions.text: One digging in the rose garden?

parts.words: One digging in the rose garden?
parts.note: sounds like a gardener, but describes a prickle on a rose stem that digs into the skin

explanation.surface: Someone at work in a flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digging' suggests a gardener; the thing digging in is a sharp spike on the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose stems carry sharp prickles that dig into anyone handling them.

clue.text: People have them transported!

parts.note: suggests goods being shipped, but being transported also means being carried away with delight

explanation.surface: People get things shipped somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' means enraptured, not moved by vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptures and states of overwhelming joy leave a person feeling carried away.

clue.text: A country expression, one might say

definitions.text: A country expression, one might say

parts.words: A country expression, one might say
parts.note: a turn of phrase peculiar to a particular nation or its language

explanation.surface: A rural saying someone might use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' suggests rural, but means a nation whose language has its own phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase whose meaning is particular to a language or region is a local expression.

clue.text: Had lots of these emperors of Rome

definitions.text: Had lots of these emperors of Rome

parts.words: Had lots of these emperors of Rome
parts.note: the Roman emperors commanded many large army units of several thousand soldiers

explanation.surface: Roman emperors possessed many of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman army divisions of thousands of soldiers were commanded by the emperors.

clue.text: We hear, the whole body in it — no, the reverse

definitions.text: We hear, the whole body in it — no, the reverse

parts.words: We hear, the whole body in it — no, the reverse
parts.note: whole sounds like hole: not a body in a hole, but a hole in the body, an opening

explanation.surface: A muddled description of something containing an entire body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' turns 'whole' into its sound-alike 'hole'; reverse the relation and you have a hole in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in the body, such as a mouth or nostril, is a hole in it.

clue.text: Won't say he's a weightlifter, perhaps

definitions.text: Won't say he's a weightlifter, perhaps

parts.words: Won't say he's a weightlifter, perhaps
parts.note: a quiet, powerful type: someone who says nothing and could be a weightlifter

explanation.surface: A man keeps quiet about lifting weights.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase describes a taciturn, tough hero; here split into 'strong' (weightlifter) and 'silent' (won't say).
explanation.definitionFit: The stock type is a quiet, tough hero of few words and great physical power.
